question: How far do the current generic SI plant and the fixed-valve kernel disagree with measured warm Mazda shaft torque and fuel at prescribed measured intake conditions?

conditions.exhaustPressurePa: measured catalyst inlet absolute pressure, used as an explicit exhaust-reservoir proxy; unmeasured upstream header loss omitted
conditions.exhaustTemperatureK: mean measured cylinder1/2/3/4 exhaust port temperatures +273.15 K, explicit representative reservoir-temperature proxy

assumptions: Generic SI air-standard model conditioned on measured RPM/MAP/IAT, not a complete or identified Mazda digital twin.
No measured torque, fuel flow, air flow, BSFC, spark or cam phase enters a model input or inverse target.
The lab-generic-ve variant fits effective intake area only to the lab's original assumed VE surface; it does not fit measured data.
The fixed-valve variant bypasses inverse VE fitting and keeps the normalized generic valve geometry fixed.
The current gasoline plant is PFI/equivalent heat, not a DI spray or fuel-chemistry model. ECU is disabled to separate plant disagreement from guessed injector calibration.
AFR14.7, effective heat-release phase18BTDC, duration50deg, gamma1.33, rod ratio1.7, valves, friction and wall heat transfer are declared generic assumptions.
Measured coolant/oil temperatures are not gas-wall temperature. The wall remains assumed450K; no substitution of coolant for metal occurs.

Exhaust reservoir pressure uses catalyst-inlet pressure without unknown upstream header loss. Reservoir temperature uses mean cylinder1/2/3/4 port readings; these sensor proxies do not identify a uniform valve boundary.
The EPA accessory drive powered only the water pump. Generic FMEP does not identify that exact accessory boundary.
Brake torque derives from net cylinder work minus FMEP friction; net work already includes pumping. No drivetrain factor or atmospheric torque correction is applied.
Pressure phasing, knock, emissions, DI transients, acoustics and durability are not validated by this campaign.
This is an initial unfitted discrepancy measurement. All selected points are evaluation-only; there is no parameter search or claimed train/holdout calibration.

The fixed-valve-settled diagnostic uses the same physical assumptions with12 rather than3 settling cycles for every selected point; this changes numerical initialization only, without fitting any measured output.
admission: ledger residuals within explicit numerical thresholds
metricNotes: Power and BSFC are algebraically derived from torque/speed/fuel and are not independent evidence. MAPE denominators require nonzero positive measured outputs. Invalid rows are retained and excluded with coverage reported; no universal accuracy pass threshold is imposed.
